$comment: The catalogue of henri error codes. Data, not code: base/errors.js reads it, the command line maps every code to an exit status through it, src/__tests__/error-codes.spec.js checks that what the source raises and what this file declares are the same set, and website/src/content/docs/reference/errors.md is generated from it. A code is forever: rename nothing, retire an entry rather than reusing it. See CONTRIBUTING and the reference page for the shape.

areas.what: the MCP server of `henri mcp` and the running application it reads
the JSON API layer: HAL answers, the health endpoint and the optional GraphQL engine
the module graph and the boot sequence: registration, ordering, dependencies
the cache of `henri.cache`: the keys it is given, the values it is asked to keep and the backend they go to
the henri command line: arguments, the project it runs in, the commands themselves
config/<env>.json, the environment overrides and the credentials file
the mail transport, the mailers of app/mailers and their views
the model files of app/models and the schema the adapters normalize
the store adapters: loading them, starting them, talking to them
the user module: sessions, passwords, tokens and the CSRF protection
the view engines, their pages and their builds

causes: node_modules is missing in the application directory
codes.fix: Install the dependencies of the application, then ask again.
codes.what: The application cannot be started because its dependencies are not installed.

causes: the documentation was not shipped with this build of the server
a partial or corrupted install
codes.fix: Reinstall @usehenri/mcp.
codes.what: The MCP server has no documentation to serve.

causes: the application answering is older than the runtime endpoints of core
codes.fix: Upgrade @usehenri/core in the application. Until then, the file-reading tools work and the running-application ones do not.
codes.what: Something henri-shaped is answering on the port and has no runtime endpoint.

causes: no `henri server` is running and `HENRI_MCP_AUTOSTART=0` forbids starting one
codes.fix: Start the development server (`henri server`), or unset HENRI_MCP_AUTOSTART.
codes.what: A tool needs a running application and none answers.

causes: NODE_ENV is production
the application answering on the port runs in production
codes.fix: Run the application in development (NODE_ENV unset or "dev"). henri mounts no runtime endpoint in production, and the MCP server will not start one to work around it.
codes.what: The MCP server refuses to read a production application.

causes: the boot failed
the application did not answer within the time the server waits
codes.fix: Run `henri server` yourself to see what it says, or `henri doctor`.
codes.what: The MCP server started the application and it never came up.

causes: a command that boots the application on a machine that is busy
a test suite or a build that takes longer than the server waits
codes.fix: Run the command in a terminal instead: the MCP server bounds how long it waits, a terminal does not.
codes.what: A command the MCP server ran did not finish in time.

causes: a typo in the page name
a page of another henri version
codes.fix: Call the guide tool without a page to list the ones this server ships.
codes.what: There is no documentation page by that name.

causes: the application stopped while the tool was talking to it
it is listening somewhere else
a request that took longer than the server waits
codes.fix: Check that the development server is still running, and read its output: a boot that failed halfway leaves the port closed.
codes.what: The running application did not answer.

causes: a model declares `graphql` types and resolvers
a route or a render asks for a `graphql` query
the package was removed but the configuration or a model still reaches for it
codes.fix: Install the engine in the application (`npm install @usehenri/graphql`), or remove the `graphql` key from the model, the route or the render that asks for it.
codes.what: Something asked for the GraphQL engine, which @usehenri/graphql carries, and the application does not have it.

causes: `res.collection()` was given something that is not an array
it was called outside a route and no `type` was passed
codes.fix: Pass an array of records, and outside a `resources` route name the type: `res.collection(records, { type: 'tasks' })`.
codes.what: res.collection() was called with something it cannot turn into a HAL collection.

causes: `res.resource()` was given an array, a scalar or nothing
it was called outside a route and no `type` was passed
codes.fix: Pass one record (a model instance or a plain object) and use `res.collection()` for lists; outside a `resources` route name the type: `res.resource(record, { type: 'tasks' })`.
codes.what: res.resource() was called with something it cannot turn into a HAL resource.

causes: two modules of the boot graph name each other in `needs`, `after` or `before`
a longer chain of the same, through an application module
codes.fix: The message names the cycle and the declaration behind every edge of it. Drop one of those declarations, or replace a `needs` that is only about ordering with an `after`.
codes.what: The modules of the boot graph wait on each other in a circle, so nothing can start.

causes: a module the boot ceiling leaves out is named in a `needs`
a command that boots to a lower level (`henri jobs`, `henri console`) reached a module that needs a higher one
codes.fix: Lower the runlevel of the module that is needed, or run the command that boots the whole application. `henri analyze` prints the order and the level of every module.
codes.what: A module needs another one that this boot does not go far enough to load.

causes: two files in app/models, app/controllers, app/mailers or app/jobs declare the same `identity`
a file was copied and its `identity` was not changed
two files of different directories collide because `identity` defaults to the file name
codes.fix: Rename one of the two files, or give it an `identity` of its own. The message names the directory and the file that collided.
codes.what: Two files of an application directory answer to the same name.

causes: an application module and a core module share a name
the same module is registered twice, from config/modules.js and from a package
codes.fix: Rename one of them: a module's name is how it is reached (`henri.<name>`), so it has to be unique. The message names both files.
codes.what: Two modules claim the same name.

causes: a store cannot be reached, a view engine cannot start, a model is invalid
an application module of app/modules threw in its `init()`
codes.fix: Read the error underneath, which carries its own code: this one only says the boot stopped. The diagnostics name what failed, what was still running and what never started.
codes.what: A module's init() failed, so the boot stopped.

causes: a module object with no `init()`, no `name` or no `runlevel`
`needs`, `after` or `before` given something that is not a name or a list of them
`reloadable` without a `reload()`, or a `release` that is not a function
a class that does not extend the base module
codes.fix: A module extends `@usehenri/core/module`, sets a unique `name`, says where it goes (`needs`/`after`/`before` or `runlevel`) and implements `init()`. See the Modules guide.
codes.what: Something registered as a module is not shaped like one.

causes: a `needs` naming a module no package and no file provides
the module that provides it is not installed, or not registered
a typo in the name
codes.fix: Register the module that provides the name, or fix the name. The message lists every module that did load and suggests the closest one.
codes.what: A module needs another one that nothing provides.

causes: the file exports an object, a string or nothing
a function was exported that resolves to something other than an array
codes.fix: Export an array of modules -- names, classes or instances -- or a function returning one: `module.exports = ['@acme/module', new Mine()]`.
codes.what: config/modules.js did not export an array of modules.

causes: a syntax error in the file
something the file requires is missing or throws
codes.fix: The message carries the loader's own error. Fix the file, or delete it: an application without one boots with the core modules alone.
codes.what: config/modules.js exists but could not be loaded.

causes: the package was never installed
it is a devDependency and the boot runs without them
the name is misspelled
codes.fix: Install the package in the application, or remove the entry from config/modules.js.
codes.what: config/modules.js names a package that cannot be resolved from the application.

causes: the command was run from a subdirectory
the folder was never scaffolded
codes.fix: Run henri from the root of the application, or create one with `henri new <name>`.
codes.what: The working directory has no package.json, so it is not a henri application.

causes: the boot ceiling (`new Henri({ runlevel })`) is below every module
`init()` was called before anything was registered
codes.fix: Register the modules before calling `init()`, or raise the ceiling. `henri analyze` prints the level of every module.
codes.what: The boot reached init() with no module to start.

causes: the renderer's peer dependencies were never installed
an install was interrupted, or node_modules was pruned
codes.fix: Run the install command the message prints. Applications carry the packages of their own renderer and adapter: henri resolves them from the application, never from itself.
codes.what: Packages the application needs are not installed.

causes: a module pins itself with `runlevel: 9`
a negative runlevel
codes.fix: The levels go from 0 to 6. Prefer naming what the module needs (`needs`, `after`, `before`) over a numeric pin.
codes.what: A module pinned itself to a level that does not exist.

causes: @usehenri/core is not a dependency of the application
the tests run from a directory that is not the application
codes.fix: Install @usehenri/core in the application, and run the tests from its root (`henri test` does).
codes.what: @usehenri/testing could not load @usehenri/core from the application.

causes: `setup()` was never awaited
`@usehenri/testing/setup-file` is missing from the vitest `setupFiles`
a test ran after `teardown()`
codes.fix: `await setup()` in `beforeAll`, or add `@usehenri/testing/setup-file` to the `setupFiles` of the vitest configuration.
codes.what: A test helper was used before the application was booted.

causes: a key built out of `null`, `undefined` or a class instance
an empty string, an empty array, or a key holding a control character
codes.fix: Key on a string, a number, a Date, an array of them (`["user", id]`) or a plain object, or give the object a `cacheKey()` method.
codes.what: Something that cannot become a cache key was used as one.

causes: `config.cache.store` names a store without a `clear(prefix)` method
codes.fix: Delete the keys you know with `henri.cache.delete()`, or give the store a `clear(prefix)` method that removes every key of a prefix.
codes.what: The cache backend cannot do what was asked of it.

causes: a `ttl` that is not a duration
a `ttl` of `0`, or a negative one, meant as "forever"
codes.fix: Use milliseconds or a duration: `'30s'`, `'5m'`, `'2h'`, `'1d'`. Every entry has one -- there is no forever -- and `config.cache.ttl` is the default when a call says nothing.
codes.what: The lifetime given to a cache entry is not a duration.

causes: a model instance, or any other class instance, handed to `set()` or returned by a `fetch()` function
`undefined`, `NaN`, `Infinity`, a Map, a Set, a Buffer, a RegExp or a circular structure inside the value
codes.fix: The cache keeps what JSON keeps, plus `Date`. Store the plain shape you want back: `record.toJSON()`, or `henri.model.stores.default.toPlain(record)`. Cache `null` where you meant "there is nothing".
codes.what: A value was refused because it would not come back the way it went in.

causes: `henri doctor` found a problem
`henri audit` found a finding at or above `--fail-on`
codes.fix: Read the report: every check names the file and what to do. `henri audit --checks` prints the whole catalogue of checks.
codes.what: A command that checks an application found something.

causes: the target of `henri new` or a generator is already there
the file would be overwritten
codes.fix: Pick another name, delete what is there, or pass `--force` where the command takes it.
codes.what: The command would write over something that already exists.

causes: a command failed for a reason henri has no finer code for
an underlying tool exited non-zero
codes.fix: Read the message. Run the command again with `--debug=henri:*` for the details, and with `--json` for the whole error object.
codes.what: The command failed.

causes: a command that asks a question was run from a script or from CI
stdin is a pipe
codes.fix: Pass the flag that answers the question (`--yes`, `--force`, `--renderer`, ...), which the hint names.
codes.what: The command needed an answer and stdin is not a terminal.

causes: the command was run from a subdirectory of the application
the folder was never scaffolded
codes.fix: Run the command from the root of the application, or create one with `henri new <name>`.
codes.what: The directory is not a henri application.

causes: the renderer, the adapter or the test runner is missing from the application
`node_modules` is stale
codes.fix: Run the install command the message prints, then run the command again.
codes.what: The command needs a package the application does not have.

causes: an unknown command or generator
a missing or invalid argument
a flag given a value it does not accept
codes.fix: `henri help <command>` prints what the command takes. The hint of the error usually lists the accepted values.
codes.what: The command was called wrongly.

causes: the file is not a henri credentials file
what it holds decrypts to something that is not a JSON object
codes.fix: Edit it with `henri credentials:edit`, which writes the envelope henri reads. Never edit the encrypted file by hand.
codes.what: The credentials file is not shaped like one.

causes: the key does not match the file (a key from another environment, or from another machine)
the encrypted file was edited, truncated or merged by hand
codes.fix: Use the key the file was written with (`HENRI_CREDENTIALS_KEY`, or config/credentials/<env>.key), or write the credentials again with `henri credentials:edit`.
codes.what: The credentials could not be decrypted: the key is wrong, or the file was modified.

causes: a truncated key
a key with a stray newline or quotes
codes.fix: A credentials key is 64 hexadecimal characters, which is what `henri credentials:init` writes. Copy the whole of it.
codes.what: The credentials key is not 64 hexadecimal characters.

causes: the key file is gitignored and was never copied to this machine
`HENRI_CREDENTIALS_KEY` is not set in the deployment
codes.fix: Set `HENRI_CREDENTIALS_KEY`, or put config/credentials/<env>.key back. The key never belongs in a commit.
codes.what: There is a credentials file for this environment and no key to open it.

causes: `HENRI_CONFIG__port=` with nothing after the equals sign
a deployment that sets a variable it does not have a value for
codes.fix: Give the variable a value, or unset it: an empty override is never what was meant.
codes.what: An environment override is set but empty.

causes: a trailing comma, a single quote, or an unquoted key
a shell that ate the quotes of the value
codes.fix: The value of a `HENRI_CONFIG_JSON__<key>` variable is parsed as JSON. Quote it whole in the shell. The value is never echoed back: it may be a secret.
codes.what: A HENRI_CONFIG_JSON__ override is not valid JSON.

causes: `HENRI_CONFIG__` or `HENRI_CONFIG_JSON__` with nothing after the separator
codes.fix: Name the key after the prefix, `__` for every level: `HENRI_CONFIG__stores__default__url`.
codes.what: An environment override names no configuration key.

causes: a number given something that is not one
a boolean given anything but `true` or `false`
an object given something that is not a JSON object
codes.fix: The type comes from the configuration file, and from henri's schema when the file has no value at that key. Give the variable a value of that type, or use `HENRI_CONFIG_JSON__<key>` for an object.
codes.what: An environment override does not fit the type of the key it overrides.

causes: a value of the wrong type, or outside what the key accepts
a key given a shape it does not take
an environment variable or a credential overriding a key with something invalid
codes.fix: Every problem is listed at once with the key, what was expected, what arrived and where the value came from. `henri doctor` runs the same schema over every config/*.json without booting. See the Configuration reference.
codes.what: The configuration holds a value henri refuses.

causes: a typo in the key
a key that only exists in another environment's file
reading a key before the module that sets it has run
codes.fix: Use `config.has(key)` first, or `config.get(key, true)`, which answers `false` instead of throwing.
codes.what: config.get() was asked for a key the configuration does not hold.

causes: no config/<NODE_ENV>.json and no config/default.json
the file is not valid JSON
the process cannot read it
codes.fix: The boot prints every path it tried. Create config/default.json, or fix the JSON of the file that is there.
codes.what: No configuration file could be loaded.

causes: an argument that is a function, a class, a bigint or a cycle
a model instance passed whole instead of its id
codes.fix: The arguments of a job are stored as JSON: pass ids and plain values, and look the records up inside `perform()`.
codes.what: The arguments of a job cannot be stored.

causes: a step that is not a whole number
a field outside its range, or a name the parser does not know
an expression that has not five fields
codes.fix: Five fields, `minute hour day month weekday`, each a number, a name, a list, a range, a step or `*`. The message names the field that is wrong.
codes.what: A recurring job has a cron expression henri cannot read.

causes: a file of app/jobs that exports nothing
a file that exports an object without a `perform`
codes.fix: A job is `app/jobs/<name>.js` exporting `perform(args, context)`, plus the optional `queue`, `priority`, `maxAttempts`, `timeout` and `backoff`.
codes.what: A file of app/jobs is not a job.

causes: a string that is not a duration (`5 minutes`, `2h`, `30s`)
a date that is not a date
a negative or infinite number
codes.fix: `performIn()` takes milliseconds or a duration string; `performAt()` takes a Date or something Date can parse.
codes.what: A delay or a date given to the queue could not be read.

causes: a schedule with neither `cron` nor `every`
a job name no file in app/jobs answers to
arguments that are not a plain object
a cron expression that can never come round (February 30th)
codes.fix: A schedule is `{ job, cron | every, args?, queue? }` and its `job` is the name of a file in app/jobs. The message names the entry that is wrong.
codes.what: A recurring job of the configuration is not shaped like a schedule.

causes: the queue was used before the boot reached it
`jobs.start()` was never awaited outside henri
codes.fix: henri starts the queue at runlevel 4; outside henri, `await jobs.start()` first.
codes.what: The job queue was used before it was started.

causes: the application has neither app/jobs nor a `jobs` block in its configuration
@usehenri/jobs is not installed
the boot did not go far enough to start the queue
codes.fix: Install the queue (`npm install @usehenri/jobs`) and write a job with `henri generate job <name>`, or stop calling `deliverLater()`/`perform()`.
codes.what: Something asked for the job queue and the application has none.

causes: a retry or a discard aimed at a job a runner is performing right now
a runner that died holding the job and has not been recovered from yet
codes.fix: Wait for it to finish, or for `jobs.stuckAfter` to pass so the queue takes it back.
codes.what: The job is being performed and cannot be changed.

causes: a typo in `jobs.store`
a store that only exists in another environment
codes.fix: Set `jobs.store` to one of the names of the `stores` block, or leave it out to use the default store.
codes.what: The queue names a store the configuration does not hold.

causes: a job whose `perform()` never returned in time
codes.fix: Raise the job’s `timeout`, or split the work: the attempt is failed and retried like any other failure.
codes.what: An attempt ran past the job’s timeout.

causes: the job was renamed or deleted while rows for it were still in the queue
a typo in the name given to `perform()`
codes.fix: `henri jobs list` shows what is queued and `app/jobs` holds the names. Discard the rows of a job that is gone with `henri jobs:discard`.
codes.what: The queue was asked to perform a job no file in app/jobs answers to.

causes: a typo in the state given to `henri jobs list --state`
codes.fix: The message lists the states a job can be in.
codes.what: The queue was asked for a state that does not exist.

causes: a store whose adapter the queue has no statements for
an adapter that reports a dialect the queue does not know
codes.fix: The queue runs on sqlite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MSSQL and MongoDB. Point `jobs.store` at a store on one of them.
codes.what: The store the queue was given cannot back it.

causes: the message returned by the mailer action is not an object
an action that returns nothing
codes.fix: A mailer action returns the message it wants sent: `return { to, subject, data }`. Everything else it holds is passed to nodemailer.
codes.what: A mailer action did not return a message.

causes: `mail` is missing from the configuration
the mail module never started, or its transport failed to verify
codes.fix: Set `mail` in the configuration -- nodemailer transport options, or `"test"` for an Ethereal account. See the Mail guide.
codes.what: A message was sent and no transport was ever built.

causes: `mail` set to a string other than `"test"`
`mail` set to a number, an array or `true`
codes.fix: `mail` takes the options object nodemailer's `createTransport()` takes, or the string `"test"`.
codes.what: The mail configuration is not a nodemailer transport.

causes: a typo in the action name
a function the mailer does not export (`defaults` and `previews` are not actions)
codes.fix: Every exported function of app/mailers/<name>.js is an action. The message lists the ones this mailer has.
codes.what: A mailer has no such action.

causes: a typo in the mailer name
the file is not in app/mailers
the file throws when it loads, so the mailer never registered
codes.fix: Mailers are the files of app/mailers, reached as `henri.mailers.<name>.<action>()`. The message lists the ones that loaded.
codes.what: There is no such mailer in app/mailers.

causes: the view was never written
it sits somewhere other than app/views/mailers
its name does not match the action
codes.fix: Write app/views/mailers/<mailer>/<action>.hbs. A `<action>.text.hbs` next to it replaces the plain text part, which is otherwise derived from the html.
codes.what: A mail has no view to render.

causes: a field with `required`, `default` or `unique` and no `type`
a field written as `{ required: true }` instead of `{ type: 'string', required: true }`
codes.fix: Every field of a henri schema names its type: `title: { type: 'string', required: true }`, or the short form `title: 'string'`.
codes.what: A model field carries options but no type.

causes: `enum` given something that is not an array
an option the adapter does not know
a relation pointing at a model that does not exist
codes.fix: The message names the field and what it holds. See the Models guide for the keys a field takes: `type`, `required`, `default`, `enum`, `unique`, `index`.
codes.what: A model field holds something the adapter refuses.

causes: no `stores.default` in the configuration
the model was written before the store was configured
codes.fix: Configure `stores.default`, or give the model a `store` naming one of the stores that exist.
codes.what: A model has no store and there is no default one.

causes: a typo in the model's `store`
a store that only exists in another environment's configuration
codes.fix: Add the store to `stores` in the configuration of this environment, or point the model at one that is there.
codes.what: A model names a store the configuration does not hold.

causes: a type of the underlying ORM rather than henri's (`STRING`, `varchar`, `ObjectId`)
a typo in the type name
codes.fix: henri's types are `string`, `text`, `number`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `date`, `json` and `uuid`. The adapter maps them to the ORM's own.
codes.what: A model field asks for a type henri does not have.

causes: a stray space in the route (`'tasks #index'`)
a character that is not a letter, a digit, a dash or an underscore
a `/` meant as a separator rather than a directory
codes.fix: An action name is letters, digits and underscores after the `#`: `'/tasks': 'tasks#index'`.
codes.what: A route points at something that is not an action name.

causes: a stray space in the route (`' tasks#index'`)
a character that is not a letter, a digit, a dash or an underscore
codes.fix: A controller name is letters, digits, dashes and underscores, with `/` for a directory: `'admin/tasks#index'`.
codes.what: A route points at something that is not a controller name.

causes: the adapter package is not installed
an install was interrupted, or node_modules is stale
the package throws when it loads
codes.fix: Install the adapter in the application (`npm install @usehenri/<adapter>`): henri resolves it from the application, never from itself.
codes.what: The adapter a store asks for cannot be loaded.

causes: the store was never started, or it was stopped
a query that outlived `henri.stop()`
a model used before the boot reached the models
codes.fix: Let the boot finish before querying. In tests, `await setup()` first; the helper boots the application inside the worker.
codes.what: A store was used before it was started, or after it was stopped.

causes: the store's adapter has no session store
the store is not loaded
the adapter's session store failed to build its table
codes.fix: Point the sessions at a store whose adapter has one (mongoose, disk, or a SQL store). Without one, sessions fall back to an in-memory store that is lost on every restart.
codes.what: No session store could be built for the user module.

causes: the server is not running, or not reachable from here
the credentials are wrong
the database does not exist
the driver of the dialect is not installed
codes.fix: The adapter's own error is underneath. Check the url of the store, that the server is up (`pnpm db:up` in development) and that the driver is installed.
codes.what: A store could not be started.

causes: a typo in `stores.<name>.adapter`
an adapter name that is not one henri knows
codes.fix: The adapters are `disk`, `mongoose`, `mysql`, `mariadb`, `postgresql`, `mssql` and `drizzle`.
codes.what: A store names an adapter henri does not have.

causes: the store is named in `api.idempotency.store` or `rateLimit.store` and the module cannot be loaded
the module does not export the shape the feature expects
codes.fix: A shared store is a module the application resolves, exporting `{ get, set, delete }`. Without one, the feature keeps its state in memory, which is wrong behind more than one process.
codes.what: A store the configuration points at could not be used.

causes: neither `url` nor `host` is set on the store
DATABASE_URL is not set in this environment
the credentials that hold the url could not be opened
codes.fix: Set `stores.<name>.url`, or the `host`, `port`, `database`, `username` and `password` the adapter assembles one from. `DATABASE_URL` sets `stores.default.url`.
codes.what: A store has nothing to connect to.

causes: a hash made with argon2id on a machine that has @node-rs/argon2, verified on one that does not
a hash bound to its record passed to compare() on its own
codes.fix: Install @node-rs/argon2 wherever the hashes are verified, and pass the user rather than the hash (`henri.user.compare(password, user)`) when password binding is on.
codes.what: A password hash cannot be checked here.

causes: no `secret` in the configuration and no `HENRI_SECRET` in the environment
a deployment that never got the variable
codes.fix: Set `HENRI_SECRET`, or `secret` in the configuration, or put it in the credentials (`henri credentials:edit`). It signs the sessions and the tokens: a new one logs everybody out.
codes.what: There is a user model and no secret to sign its sessions with.

causes: the user module ended up in a boot that has no server
a module ordering that puts the user module before the express app
codes.fix: Do not pin the user module below the server. A boot that stops before the server (`henri jobs`, `henri console`) does not mount sessions at all.
codes.what: The user module needs the express app and there is none.

causes: a token asked for without a secret, a purpose or a subject
the application signs its own tokens and left one of the three out
codes.fix: A henri token is signed with the configuration's `secret` and carries a purpose and a subject; all three are required.
codes.what: A token could not be signed.

causes: the renderer's own build failed (a page that does not compile, a missing import)
the build ran without the packages the renderer needs
codes.fix: The bundler's own output is above the error. Run `henri build` again after fixing it; the development server prints the same errors as it reloads.
codes.what: The view engine's build did not finish.

causes: @usehenri/inertia, @inertiajs/react, react, react-dom or vite is not installed
the package throws when it loads
codes.fix: Install the renderer in the application: `npm install @usehenri/inertia @inertiajs/react react react-dom vite @vitejs/plugin-react`.
codes.what: The configuration asks for the inertia renderer and the application does not have it.

causes: a renderer that is not a henri view engine
a version of the engine older than the core running it
codes.fix: `henri build` calls `build({ cwd, config })` on the engine. A view engine implements `init`, `prepare`, `fallback`, `render` and, to be buildable, `build`.
codes.what: The view engine has no build() to call.

causes: the application was never scaffolded, or its views were moved
a build run from somewhere other than the root of the application
codes.fix: The renderer reads its pages from app/views/pages. Run the command from the root of the application, or scaffold one with `henri new`.
codes.what: The renderer has no pages directory to render or to build.

causes: @usehenri/react, next, react or react-dom is not installed
the package throws when it loads
codes.fix: Install the renderer in the application: `npm install @usehenri/react next react react-dom`. New applications get the inertia renderer instead.
codes.what: The configuration asks for the react renderer and the application does not have it.

causes: the server bundle was not built (`henri build` before serving with ssr on)
the bundle does not export `render()`
a page that throws when it renders on the server
codes.fix: Build the server bundle, or turn server-side rendering off (`inertia.ssr: false`) while the page is fixed.
codes.what: Server-side rendering failed.

causes: a typo in `renderer`
a renderer that is experimental and not enabled
codes.fix: `renderer` takes `inertia`, `react` or `template`. An experimental one is enabled with `"experimental": { "<name>": true }`.
codes.what: The configuration asks for a renderer henri does not have.

causes: `renderer: "vue"` without the experimental flag
codes.fix: Enable it with `"experimental": { "vue": true }`. It was written for Nuxt 2 and has not been exercised since 2020: prefer `inertia`.
codes.what: The vue renderer is experimental and was not enabled.
